elements.element: Licence/access rights extend to Customer's affiliates
Licence/access rights extend to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf"

elements.element: Paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: No paid-up licence is granted in Section 1.4 (hosting access and administration tool access only); the condition is demonstrably absent

elements.element: Subscription/ongoing licence terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: "shall not be suspended or revoked by HDI except upon termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 4" — Section 4's grounds are not shown, so it may permit termination other than for uncured material breach
"may be exercised by any successor to the Company's business (including in a merger or acquisition)"
"extend to the Company's affiliates" — granted unconditionally, exceeding the notice-conditioned fallback

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "any successor to the Company's business (including in a merger or acquisition)"

offending_extra_words: HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.
reasons: The added sentence secures affiliates, contractors, successor transferability and non-revocation, but the anti-revocation hook points to "termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 4" rather than to uncured material breach, so the preferred limit on terminating the ongoing right cannot be confirmed; use "except for the Company's uncured material breach" (or reference the breach-termination subsection) to lock the preferred level.
No paid-up licence exists in Section 1.4, so the perpetual/irrevocable element is inapplicable rather than deficient.
The clause comfortably clears the fallback: affiliates are covered without any notice condition and the rights expressly pass to an M&A successor.

Minimality fails on operation form: the edit re-states the entire existing second sentence verbatim inside the replacement (26 words expanded to 88; changed-character ratio 0.683), when a standalone appended sentence would have achieved the same result without touching existing operative text.

Intent is preserved — the bandwidth, burst-capacity and administration-tool obligations remain effective and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced (Section 4 is an existing cross-reference).
